title: Does anyone really care about me? - God the Creator who is love
summary: A first encounter with the God who knows me personally, made me out of love, and cares about my everyday life - the starting point for a relationship, not religion.

sections.heading: Is there Anyone who cares about me?

items.comment: Before we ask "does God exist?", the Psalm asks something else: whether anyone truly knows me. God knows every thought and word before I speak it.

questions.text: How do you feel reading that Someone knows you this thoroughly - uneasy or relieved? Why?

items.comment: I am not an accident or a mistake - I was "knitted together" and written in God's book before I had done anything.

questions.text: What changes in how you see yourself if you exist by design rather than by chance?

items.comment: Against the vastness of the universe a human seems small - yet God remembers him and crowns him with dignity.

questions.text: When did you last feel "small" or unimportant? How does the Psalm answer that?

items.comment: The Bible doesn't only say God loves - it says God *is* love, and the proof is that He came to us first.

questions.text: What is the difference between "God loves" and "God is love"?

items.comment: God's love has a concrete address - the world, which means me too - and a concrete cost: the Son.

questions.text: If you put your own name in place of "the world," how would this verse read for you?

items.comment: God did not wait until I improved. He showed His love *while* I was still turned away from Him.

questions.text: What does this mean for someone who thinks they must first "earn" God's love?

items.comment: God's love is not a passing feeling - it is "everlasting," persistent, seeking.

questions.text: What does it mean that someone loves you with an "everlasting love," not one dependent on your form?

items.comment: In the parable the father runs out first - a picture of a God who does not wait with folded arms.

questions.text: Which move is the surprising one here: the son's return or the father's run? Why?

sections.heading: He cares about my everyday life

items.comment: If God feeds the birds, He cares about you all the more - you are more valuable than they are.

questions.text: What do you worry about most? How does awareness of God's care change that?

items.comment: God does not promise a life without needs, but a Father who "knows," and He invites us to seek Him first.

questions.text: What would "seeking the Kingdom first" look like practically in your week?

items.comment: Worry can be "cast" on God - because He genuinely cares about you.

questions.text: What is one worry you would like to "cast" on God today?

items.comment: Counted hairs are an image of attention to the smallest detail of your life.

questions.text: Is it easier for you to trust a God "of big things" or a God attentive to small details?

items.comment: Humans are made "in the image of God" - hence their unique worth and capacity for relationship.

questions.text: If I bear "God's image," what does that say about the worth of every person, including mine?

items.comment: God calls by name and says "you are mine" - the language of relationship, not anonymous religion.

questions.text: What would it mean to hear God speak your own name and the words "you are mine"?

items.comment: God the Creator is not far off - "in Him we live and move and have our being," and He wants to be found.

questions.text: What in this text shows that God is near, even though we don't see Him?

items.comment: The goal of this love is not admiration from a distance, but being called children of God.

questions.text: What changes in the relationship with God when we move from "Creator" to "Father"?

items.label: "God is love" (1 John 4:8)
items.content: In Greek "love" here is *agapē* - self-giving love that chooses the good of the other, not dependent on merit. The statement "God is love" describes not only what God does, but who He is.

questions.text: How does understanding *agapē* as choosing love (rather than reciprocated love) change the picture of God?

items.label: "image of God" (Gen 1:27)
items.content: The Hebrew *tselem* ("image") stresses that the human being represents God within creation and is called to relationship with Him - the foundation of human dignity.

items.label: Psalm 139 as comfort, not threat
items.content: God's omniscience and omnipresence in Ps 139 are presented not as surveillance but as the care of One who knows and does not abandon. This is the interpretive key to the whole psalm. ---

application.text: God is not a distant judge or an impersonal force. He knows you by name, made you by design and out of love, and cares about your everyday life. Faith does not begin with an effort to earn - it begins with accepting that you are wanted and loved.
application.challenge: Over the coming week, write down each day one thing in which you notice God's care for you. Once this week, "cast" one specific worry on God (1 Pet 5:7) - tell Him directly.
